title: Born on September 10th, the man who redrew India's map along language lines.
caption:
Born on September 10th, the man who redrew India's map along language lines.

Born in a small village near Almora in the United Provinces, Pant trained as a lawyer before joining India's independence movement alongside Gandhi, Nehru and Patel. He was jailed twice by the British - once for organizing the Satyagraha movement, once for signing the Quit India resolution.

After independence, Pant became Uttar Pradesh's first Chief Minister, abolishing the zamindari land system. As Union Home Minister from 1955, his defining achievement was reorganizing India's states along linguistic lines - the map India still largely uses today.

Pant received the Bharat Ratna in 1957 and died in office in 1961. Nearly seven decades later, the state boundaries he helped draw still shape how India governs itself - proof that the unglamorous work of institution-building compounds longer than almost anything else.
